name: glyph
doc: Package glyph provides a terminal UI framework for Go.

types.name: Align
types.doc: Align specifies text alignment within a cell.
types.decl: type Align uint8

examples.doc:
Text alignment.
Align is set via the Style struct. AlignLeft, AlignCenter, or AlignRight within a fixed width.
examples.code:
VBox(
	Text("left-aligned"),
	Text("centered").Style(Style{Align: AlignCenter}).Width(40),
	Text("right-aligned").Style(Style{Align: AlignRight}).Width(40),
)

types.name: AnchorPosition
types.doc: AnchorPosition defines how an overlay is positioned relative to a NodeRef
types.decl: type AnchorPosition int

consts.decl:
const (
	AnchorNone    AnchorPosition = iota
	AnchorBelow                  // top of overlay at bottom of ref
	AnchorAbove                  // bottom of overlay at top of ref
	AnchorOnTop                  // overlay covers the ref exactly
	AnchorRightOf                // left edge of overlay at right edge of ref
	AnchorLeftOf                 // right edge of overlay at left edge of ref
)

types.name: AnimateFn
types.doc:
AnimateFn configures and creates tweens. Methods return new AnimateFn values,
so animation styles can be defined once and reused across properties:

	smooth := Animate.Duration(200 * time.Millisecond).Ease(EaseOutCubic)
	VBox.Height(smooth(&targetHeight))
	VBox.Width(smooth(&targetWidth))
	Sparkline(data).Height(smooth(If(&expanded).Then(int16(26)).Else(int16(1))))
types.decl: type AnimateFn func(target any) *tween

methods.name: Duration
methods.doc: Duration sets the animation duration. Returns a new AnimateFn.

methods.name: Ease
methods.doc:
Ease sets the easing function. Receives t in [0,1], returns eased t in [0,1].
Returns a new AnimateFn.
methods.signature: func (f AnimateFn) Ease(fn func(float64) float64) AnimateFn

methods.name: From
methods.doc:
From sets the initial value before animation starts.
The tween immediately begins interpolating from this value toward the target.
Returns a new AnimateFn.

	SEVignette().Strength(Animate.Duration(1*time.Second).From(0.0)(0.88))

methods.name: OnComplete
methods.doc: OnComplete sets a callback that fires once when the animation reaches its target.

vars.doc:
Animate creates a tween that watches a target value and interpolates toward it.
target can be a pointer (*int16, *float32, etc.), a conditionNode, or any
value the property compiler can resolve to a typed pointer.

	// simple — uses defaults (200ms linear)
	VBox.Height(Animate(&targetHeight))

	// configured up-front, applied to target
	Animate.Duration(300 * time.Millisecond).Ease(EaseOutCubic)(&targetHeight)

examples.doc:
Animation tween.
Animate interpolates toward a target value over time. Configure duration and easing, then apply to any numeric property.
examples.code:
smooth := Animate.Duration(300 * time.Millisecond).Ease(EaseOutCubic)

var h int16 = 5
VBox.Height(smooth(&h)).Border(BorderRounded)(
	Text("animated"),
)

examples.name: color
examples.doc:
Colour tween.
Animate works on Color pointers. The colour lerps through RGB space toward the target.
examples.code:
fg := Red
VBox.Border(BorderRounded)(
	Text("status").FG(Animate.Duration(500 * time.Millisecond)(&fg)),
)

examples.name: conditional
examples.doc:
Conditional target.
Wrap a conditional in Animate — the tween triggers whenever the condition changes.
examples.code:
expanded := true
smooth := Animate.Duration(300 * time.Millisecond).Ease(EaseOutCubic)

VBox.Height(smooth(If(&expanded).Then(int16(5)).Else(int16(1)))).Border(BorderRounded)(
	Text("content"),
)

examples.name: onComplete
examples.doc:
Completion callback.
OnComplete fires once when the animation reaches its target value.

types.name: App
types.doc: App is a TUI application with integrated input handling via riffkey.

constructors.name: NewApp
constructors.doc: NewApp creates a new TUI application (fullscreen, alternate buffer).

examples.doc:
Full-screen app.
SetView compiles the tree once. On declares key bindings in the tree. Run blocks until Stop is called.
examples.code:
app := NewApp()
app.SetView(VBox(
	Text("hello from glyph"),
	Text("press q to quit"),
	On(Key("q", func() { app.Stop() })),
))
app.Run()
examples.output:
hello from glyph
press q to quit

constructors.name: NewInlineApp
constructors.doc:
NewInlineApp creates a new inline TUI application.
Inline apps render at the current cursor position without taking over the screen.
Use this for progress bars, selection menus, spinners, etc.

examples.doc:
Inline app.
Renders within the terminal flow instead of taking over the screen. Height sets the visible rows.
examples.code:
app := NewInlineApp()

status := "loading..."
app.SetView(Text(&status))
app.Height(3).ClearOnExit(true)
app.Run()

methods.name: AddEffect
methods.doc:
AddEffect appends a post-processing pass to the pipeline.
Passes run in order after template rendering, before screen flush.
Closures captured by the pass act as shader uniforms — mutate them to
change behaviour next frame.

methods.name: AddJumpTarget
methods.doc:
AddJumpTarget registers a jump target during rendering.
Called by Jump components when jump mode is active.
methods.signature: func (a *App) AddJumpTarget(x, y int16, onSelect func(), style Style)

methods.name: Back
methods.doc:
Back returns to the previous view.
Currently an alias for Pop().

methods.name: BindField
methods.doc: BindField routes unmatched keys to a text input field.

methods.name: ClearOnExit
methods.doc:
ClearOnExit sets whether the inline app should clear its content on exit.
If true, the rendered content disappears when the app stops.
If false (default), the content remains visible and cursor moves below it.

methods.name: Cursor
methods.doc: Cursor returns the current cursor state.

methods.name: EnterJumpMode
methods.doc:
EnterJumpMode activates jump label mode.
A render is triggered to collect jump targets, then a temporary router
is pushed to handle label input.

methods.name: ExitJumpMode
methods.doc: ExitJumpMode deactivates jump label mode.

methods.name: Go
methods.doc:
Go switches to a different view.
Swaps the template and input handlers.

methods.name: Handle
methods.doc:
Handle registers a key binding with a vim-style pattern.
Examples: "j", "gg", "<C-c>", "<C-w>j", "<Up>"
Accepts func(riffkey.Match), func(any), or func() for convenience.
Automatically requests a re-render after the handler runs.

methods.name: HandleNamed
methods.doc:
HandleNamed registers a named key binding (for rebinding support).
Automatically requests a re-render after the handler runs.
methods.signature: func (a *App) HandleNamed(name, pattern string, handler func(riffkey.Match)) *App

methods.name: Height
methods.doc:
Height sets the height for inline apps.
This determines how many lines the inline view will use.
If not set, defaults to 1.

methods.name: HideCursor
methods.doc: HideCursor hides the cursor.

methods.name: Input
methods.doc: Input returns the riffkey input for modal handling (push/pop).

methods.name: IsInline
methods.doc: IsInline returns true if this is an inline app.

methods.name: JumpKey
methods.doc:
JumpKey registers a key pattern to trigger jump mode.
This is a convenience method that calls EnterJumpMode when the key is pressed.

methods.name: JumpMode
methods.doc: JumpMode returns the jump mode state for use during rendering.

methods.name: JumpModeActive
methods.doc: JumpModeActive returns true if jump mode is currently active.

methods.name: JumpStyle
methods.doc: JumpStyle returns the current jump style.

methods.name: OnAfterRender
methods.doc:
OnAfterRender sets a callback to be called after each render completes.
Use this to update cursor position after layout is known.

methods.name: OnBeforeRender
methods.doc:
OnBeforeRender sets a callback to be called before each render.
Use this to sync state (e.g., filter updates) before layout runs.

methods.name: OnResize
methods.doc:
OnResize sets a callback to be called when the terminal is resized.
The callback receives the new width and height.
Use this to update viewport dimensions, reinitialize layers, etc.

methods.name: Pop
methods.doc: Deprecated: use PopRouter instead.

methods.name: PopRouter
methods.doc: PopRouter pops the current router from the input stack.

methods.name: PopView
methods.doc:
PopView removes the top modal overlay.
Returns to the previous view in the stack.

methods.name: Push
methods.doc: Deprecated: use PushRouter instead.

methods.name: PushRouter
methods.doc: PushRouter pushes a new router onto the input stack (for modal input).

methods.name: PushView
methods.doc:
PushView pushes a view as a modal overlay.
The modal's handlers take precedence until PopView() is called.
The pushed view becomes the active rendered view until popped.

methods.name: Ref
methods.doc: Ref provides access to the component for external references.

methods.name: RenderNow
methods.doc:
RenderNow performs a render immediately without channel coordination.
Use this from dedicated update goroutines to avoid scheduler overhead.
The render is mutex-protected so it's safe to call concurrently.

methods.name: RequestRender
methods.doc:
RequestRender marks that a render is needed.
Safe to call from any goroutine.

methods.name: Router
methods.doc: Router returns the riffkey router for advanced configuration.

methods.name: Run
methods.doc:
Run starts the application. Blocks until Stop is called.
For multi-view apps, use RunFrom(startView) instead.

methods.name: RunFrom
methods.doc:
RunFrom starts the application on the specified view.
Use this for multi-view apps.

methods.name: RunNonInteractive
methods.doc:
RunNonInteractive runs an inline app without an input loop.
Use this for progress bars, spinners, etc. that don't need keyboard input.
Call Stop() when done to clean up and exit.

methods.name: Screen
methods.doc: Screen returns the screen.

methods.name: SetCursor
methods.doc:
SetCursor sets the cursor position (0-indexed screen coordinates).
The cursor will be positioned here after each render.

methods.name: SetCursorStyle
methods.doc: SetCursorStyle sets the cursor visual style.

methods.name: SetDefaultStyle
methods.doc:
SetCursorColor sets the cursor color using OSC 12 escape sequence.
This changes the actual cursor color in supporting terminals.
SetDefaultStyle sets the default style for all cells. Any cell not explicitly
styled will use this FG/BG instead of the terminal default.

methods.name: SetEffect
methods.doc:
SetEffect replaces the entire post-processing pipeline.
Call with no arguments to clear all passes.

methods.name: SetJumpStyle
methods.doc: SetJumpStyle sets the global style for jump labels.

methods.name: SetView
SetViewLimit
methods.doc:
SetViewLimit sets the maximum number of times SetView can be called.
Panics if exceeded. Use this to catch anti-patterns where SetView is called
repeatedly instead of using reactive updates via pointers.

Example:

	app.SetViewLimit(1) // Panic if SetView called more than once
	app.SetView(myView) // OK
	app.SetView(other)  // PANIC: SetView called 2 times, limit is 1

Set to 0 (default) for unlimited calls.

methods.name: ShowCursor
methods.doc: ShowCursor makes the cursor visible.

methods.name: Size
methods.doc: Size returns the current screen size.

methods.name: Stop
methods.doc: Stop signals the application to stop.

methods.name: Template
methods.doc:
Template returns the current template for debugging.
Use with Template().DebugDump("") to inspect the op tree.

methods.name: UnbindField
methods.doc: UnbindField clears the text input field binding.

methods.name: UpdateView
methods.doc:
UpdateView recompiles a view with a new view definition.
Use this when the view's structure changes and needs re-compilation.

methods.name: View
methods.doc:
View registers a named view for multi-view routing.
Returns a builder for chaining Handle() calls.

Example:

	app.View("home", homeView).
	    Handle("j", moveDown).
	    Handle("s", func(_ riffkey.Match) { app.Go("settings") })

methods.name: ViewRouter
methods.doc:
ViewRouter returns the router for a named view, if it exists.
Useful for advanced configuration like HandleUnmatched.

examples.name: goroutine
examples.doc:
Background updates.
Mutate state, then call RequestRender to trigger a redraw.
examples.code:
app := NewApp()

status := "waiting..."
app.SetView(VBox(
	Text(&status),
	On(Key("q", func() { app.Stop() })),
))

time.AfterFunc(2*time.Second, func() {
	status = "done!"
	app.RequestRender()
})

app.Run()

examples.name: multiView
examples.doc:
Multi-view routing.
Named views with per-view key bindings. Go switches between views; each view is compiled independently.
examples.code:
app := NewApp()

app.View("home", VBox(
	Text("Welcome"),
	Text("press n for next"),
	On(Key("n", func() { app.Go("detail") })),
))

app.View("detail", VBox(
	Text("Detail view"),
	Text("press b for back"),
	On(Key("b", func() { app.Go("home") })),
))

app.RunFrom("home")

types.name: Attribute
types.doc: Attribute represents text styling attributes that can be combined.
types.decl: type Attribute uint8

methods.name: Has
methods.doc: Has returns true if the attribute set contains the given attribute.

methods.name: With
methods.doc: With returns a new attribute set with the given attribute added.

methods.name: Without
methods.doc: Without returns a new attribute set with the given attribute removed.

consts.decl:
const (
	AttrNone Attribute = 0
	AttrBold Attribute = 1 << iota
	AttrDim
	AttrItalic
	AttrUnderline
	AttrBlink
	AttrInverse
	AttrStrikethrough
)

types.name: AutoTableC

constructors.name: AutoTable
constructors.doc:
AutoTable creates a table directly from a slice of structs.
Pass a plain slice for a static snapshot, or a pointer (&items) for reactive updates.
Columns are derived from exported struct fields; use .Columns() to select and order them.

examples.doc:
Struct table.
Generate a table from a struct slice. Column options control formatting.

examples.name: columns
examples.doc:
Column formatters.
Mix formatters: percentages, byte sizes, booleans, and colour-coded changes.
examples.code:
type Service struct {
	Name   string
	CPU    float64
	Memory uint64
	Active bool
	Growth float64
}
rows := []Service{
	{Name: "api", CPU: 82.3, Memory: 1073741824, Active: true, Growth: 0.12},
}
AutoTable(&rows).
	Column("CPU", FormatPercent(1)).
	Column("Memory", FormatBytes()).
	Column("Active", FormatBool("Yes", "No")).
	Column("Growth", FormatPercentChange(1))
examples.output:
Name            CPU       Memory    Active          Growth
api           82.3%       1.0 GB     Yes             +0.1%

methods.name: AltRowStyle
methods.doc: AltRowStyle sets the alternating row style.

methods.name: BindNav
methods.doc:
BindNav registers key bindings for scrolling down/up by one row.
the closures capture the scroll pointer and data pointer, reading the
current slice length at invocation time for correct clamping.
methods.signature: func (t AutoTableC) BindNav(down, up string) AutoTableC

methods.name: BindPageNav
methods.doc: BindPageNav registers key bindings for page-sized scrolling.
methods.signature: func (t AutoTableC) BindPageNav(pageDown, pageUp string) AutoTableC

methods.name: BindVimNav
methods.doc:
BindVimNav wires standard vim-style scroll keys:
j/k for line, Ctrl-d/Ctrl-u for page.

methods.name: Border
methods.doc: Border sets the border style.

methods.name: Column
methods.doc:
Column configures rendering for a specific column by struct field name.
The option can be a canned preset or a custom function:

	AutoTable(&data).
	    Column("Price", FormatCurrency("$", 2)).
	    Column("Change", FormatPercentChange(1)).
	    Column("Active", func(c *ColumnConfig) {
	        c.Align(AlignCenter)
	        c.Format(func(v any) string { ... })
	    })
methods.signature: func (t AutoTableC) Column(name string, opt ColumnOption) AutoTableC

methods.name: Columns
methods.doc:
Columns selects which struct fields to display and in what order.
Field names are case-sensitive and must match exported struct fields.

methods.name: Gap
methods.doc: Gap sets the spacing between columns. Accepts int8, int, or *int8 for dynamic values.

methods.name: HeaderStyle
methods.doc: HeaderStyle sets the header row style.

methods.name: Headers
methods.doc:
Headers sets custom header labels for the columns.
Must be called after Columns() and have the same number of entries.

methods.name: Margin
methods.doc: Margin sets uniform margin on all sides.

methods.name: MarginTRBL
methods.doc: MarginTRBL sets individual margins for top, right, bottom, left.
methods.signature: func (t AutoTableC) MarginTRBL(a, b, c, d int16) AutoTableC

methods.name: MarginVH
methods.doc: MarginVH sets vertical and horizontal margin.
methods.signature: func (t AutoTableC) MarginVH(v, h int16) AutoTableC

methods.name: RowStyle
methods.doc: RowStyle sets the default row style.

methods.name: Scrollable
methods.doc:
Scrollable enables viewport scrolling with the given maximum visible rows.
renders all data rows to an internal buffer, blits only the visible window.

methods.name: SortBy
methods.doc:
SortBy sets the default sort column and direction. implies Sortable().
field is the struct field name (e.g. "CPU"). asc true = ascending.
methods.signature: func (t AutoTableC) SortBy(field string, asc bool) AutoTableC

methods.name: Sortable
methods.doc:
Sortable enables column sorting via jump labels.
when the app's jump key is pressed, each column header becomes a jump target.
selecting a column sorts ascending; selecting the same column again toggles direction.

types.name: BlendMode
types.doc:
BlendMode controls how two colours are combined during post-processing.
Use with WithBlend to wrap any Effect effect.
types.decl: type BlendMode int

consts.decl:
const (
	BlendNormal    BlendMode = iota
	BlendMultiply            // darkens: a * b / 255
	BlendScreen              // lightens: 255 - (255-a)(255-b)/255
	BlendOverlay             // multiply if dark, screen if light
	BlendAdd                 // clipped addition
	BlendSoftLight           // gentle contrast
	BlendDodge               // dramatic brighten
	BlendBurn                // dramatic darken
)

types.name: BloomEffect
types.doc: BloomEffect creates a coloured glow around bright cells.

constructors.name: SEBloom
constructors.doc:
SEBloom creates a coloured glow around bright cells.
Bleeds bright colours into both FG and BG of surrounding cells.
Default: radius 2, threshold 0.6, strength 0.3.

examples.doc: Bloom around bright cells.
examples.code:
VBox(
	VBox.Border(BorderRounded)(
		HBox(
			Text("████").FG(RGB(255, 255, 200)),
			Text("    "),
			Text("████").FG(RGB(200, 255, 255)),
		),
		Text("dim text").FG(RGB(60, 60, 60)),
		Text("bright cells glow outward").FG(RGB(200, 196, 184)),
	),
	ScreenEffect(SEBloom().Threshold(0.6).Strength(0.3)),
)

examples.name: focus
examples.doc: Bloom constrained to a panel.
examples.code:
var panel NodeRef
VBox(
	HBox(
		Text("████").FG(RGB(255, 255, 200)),
		Text(" no bloom here "),
	),
	VBox.Border(BorderRounded).NodeRef(&panel)(
		Text("████").FG(RGB(255, 255, 200)),
		Text("bloom only here").FG(RGB(200, 196, 184)),
	),
	ScreenEffect(SEBloom().Focus(&panel)),
)

methods.name: Focus
methods.doc: Focus constrains bloom output to the given node — only cells within the rect receive glow.

methods.name: Radius
methods.doc: Radius sets the spread in cells (2-4 recommended).

methods.name: Strength
methods.doc: Strength sets glow intensity (0.3 = subtle, 1.0 = vivid).

methods.name: Threshold
methods.doc: Threshold sets the minimum brightness that blooms (0.0–1.0).

types.name: BoolValidator
types.doc:
BoolValidator validates a boolean value. Pass to Checkbox().Validate().
Return nil for valid, non-nil error for the message to display.
types.decl: type BoolValidator func(bool) error

types.name: BorderStyle
types.doc:
BorderStyle defines the characters used for drawing borders.
Top/Bottom override Horizontal for their respective edge.
Zero-value runes are skipped, enabling partial borders.
types.decl:
type BorderStyle struct {
	Horizontal  rune
	Vertical    rune
	TopLeft     rune
	TopRight    rune
	BottomLeft  rune
	BottomRight rune
	Top         rune // overrides Horizontal for top edge
	Bottom      rune // overrides Horizontal for bottom edge
	Left        rune // overrides Vertical for left edge
	Right       rune // overrides Vertical for right edge
}

methods.name: HasBorder
methods.doc: HasBorder returns true if any edge is drawn.

methods.name: PadBottom
methods.doc: PadBottom returns 1 if the bottom edge is drawn, 0 otherwise.

methods.name: PadH
methods.doc: PadH returns total horizontal border padding (left + right).

methods.name: PadLeft
methods.doc: PadLeft returns 1 if the left edge is drawn, 0 otherwise.

methods.name: PadRight
methods.doc: PadRight returns 1 if the right edge is drawn, 0 otherwise.

methods.name: PadTop
methods.doc: PadTop returns 1 if the top edge is drawn, 0 otherwise.

methods.name: PadV
methods.doc: PadV returns total vertical border padding (top + bottom).

examples.doc:
Built-in borders.
Choose from BorderSingle, BorderRounded, or BorderDouble.

examples.name: custom
examples.doc:
Custom borders.
Define custom borders with any rune for each edge and corner.
examples.code:
ascii := BorderStyle{
	Horizontal:  '-',
	Vertical:    '|',
	TopLeft:     '+',
	TopRight:    '+',
	BottomLeft:  '+',
	BottomRight: '+',
}
VBox.Border(ascii)(Text("ascii box"))

types.name: Box
types.doc:
Box is a container with a custom layout function.
Use this when HBox/VBox don't fit your needs.

types.name: Buffer
types.doc: Buffer is a 2D grid of cells representing a drawable surface.

constructors.name: NewBuffer
constructors.doc: NewBuffer creates a new buffer with the given dimensions.

methods.name: Blit
methods.doc:
Blit copies a rectangular region from src buffer to this buffer.
srcX, srcY: top-left corner in source buffer (for scrolling)
dstX, dstY: top-left corner in destination buffer
width, height: size of region to copy
Copies row-by-row using copy().
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) Blit(src *Buffer, srcX, srcY, dstX, dstY, width, height int)

methods.name: Clear
methods.doc:
Clear clears the buffer to empty cells with default style.
Uses copy() from a cached empty buffer.

methods.name: ClearDirty
methods.doc:
ClearDirty clears only the rows that were written to since last clear.
Useful when content doesn't fill the buffer.

methods.name: ClearDirtyFlags
methods.doc:
ClearDirtyFlags resets all row dirty flags after a flush.
Call this after Screen.Flush() to start tracking changes for next frame.

methods.name: ClearLine
methods.doc: ClearLine clears a single line to empty cells.

methods.name: ClearLineWithStyle
methods.doc: ClearLineWithStyle clears a single line with a styled space cell.

methods.name: ContentHeight
methods.doc: ContentHeight returns the number of rows that have been written to.

methods.name: CopyFrom
methods.doc:
CopyFrom copies all cells from src to b using a single bulk copy.
Requires both buffers to have identical dimensions.
Uses a single bulk copy of the cell slice.

methods.name: DrawBorder
methods.doc:
DrawBorder draws a border around the given rectangle.
Zero-value runes are skipped, enabling partial borders.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) DrawBorder(x, y, width, height int, border BorderStyle, style Style)

methods.name: DrawPanel
methods.doc:
DrawPanel draws a bordered panel with title and returns the interior region.
Title appears in the top border: ┌─ TITLE ─────┐
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) DrawPanel(x, y, w, h int, title string, style Style) *Region

methods.name: DrawPanelEx
methods.doc: DrawPanelEx draws a panel with custom border style.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) DrawPanelEx(x, y, w, h int, title string, border BorderStyle, style Style) *Region

methods.name: Fill
methods.doc: Fill fills the entire buffer with the given cell.

methods.name: FillRect
methods.doc:
FillRect fills a rectangular region with the given cell.
Uses direct slice writes (no border merge) for non-border cells,
falls back to Set() only when the cell is a border character.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) FillRect(x, y, width, height int, c Cell)

methods.name: Get
methods.doc:
Get returns the cell at the given coordinates.
Returns an empty cell if out of bounds.

methods.name: GetLine
methods.doc: GetLine returns the content of a single line as a string (trimmed).

methods.name: GetLineStyled
methods.doc: GetLineStyled returns a line with embedded ANSI escape codes for styles.

methods.name: HLine
methods.doc: HLine draws a horizontal line of the given rune.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) HLine(x, y, length int, r rune, style Style)

methods.name: Height
methods.doc: Height returns the buffer height.

methods.name: InBounds
methods.doc: InBounds returns true if the given coordinates are within the buffer.

methods.name: MarkAllDirty
methods.doc:
MarkAllDirty forces all rows to be considered dirty.
Useful after external modifications or for testing.

methods.name: Region
methods.doc: Region creates a view into a rectangular region of the buffer.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) Region(x, y, width, height int) *Region

methods.name: ResetDirtyMax
methods.doc:
ResetDirtyMax resets the dirty tracking without clearing content.
Use when you know the template will overwrite all cells.

methods.name: Resize
methods.doc:
Resize resizes the buffer to new dimensions.
Existing content is preserved where it fits.

methods.name: Row
methods.doc:
Row returns a writer for row y with the style precomputed and the row marked dirty.
If y is out of bounds, Put calls on the returned writer are no-ops.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) Row(y int, style Style) RowWriter

methods.name: RowDirty
methods.doc:
RowDirty returns true if the given row has been modified since last ClearDirtyFlags.
If allDirty is set (after Clear/Resize), all rows are considered dirty.

methods.name: Set
methods.doc:
Set sets the cell at the given coordinates.
Does nothing if out of bounds.
When drawing border characters, automatically merges with existing borders.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) Set(x, y int, c Cell)

methods.name: SetFast
methods.doc:
SetFast sets a cell without border merging. Use for text/progress where
you know the content isn't a border character.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) SetFast(x, y int, c Cell)

methods.name: SetOpacity
methods.doc:
SetOpacity composites c over the existing cell using glyph's terminal
opacity rules. Default BG on c is treated as transparent and preserves the
existing cell BG; set an explicit BG when the source should fade a fill.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) SetOpacity(x, y int, c Cell, opacity float64, mode OpacityMode)

methods.name: SetRune
methods.doc: SetRune sets just the rune at the given coordinates, preserving style.
methods.signature: func (b *Buffer) SetRune(x, y int, r rune)

constructors.name: Rich
constructors.doc:
Rich creates a RichText from a mix of strings and Spans.
Plain strings get default styling, Spans keep their styling.

Example:

	Rich("Hello ", Bold("world"), "!")

Single-arg shortcut: pass a *[]Span (or []Span) to render a live span
slice. The renderer reads it every frame, so mutating the slice after
construction updates the render next frame.

	Rich(&statusSpans)  // live spans, mutate slice to update

examples.doc:
Inline spans.
Mix Bold, Dim, Italic, FG and plain strings in a single line.
examples.code:
Rich(
	Bold("Important: "),
	Dim("supporting detail "),
	FG("error", Red),
)

constructors.name: ScreenEffect
constructors.doc:
ScreenEffect creates a declarative full-screen post-processing node.
Accepts multiple effects — they apply in order, left to right.

examples.doc:
Single post-processing effect.
Place ScreenEffect anywhere in the view tree — it applies to the whole screen.
examples.code:
VBox(
	VBox.Border(BorderRounded)(
		HBox(
			Text("● online").FG(Green),
			Text("  "),
			Text("■ queue: 42").FG(Yellow),
		),
		HBox(
			Text("cpu ").FG(Cyan),
			Text("████░░░░").FG(RGB(100, 200, 255)),
		),
		Text("ready").FG(RGB(200, 196, 184)),
	),
	ScreenEffect(SEVignette()),
)

examples.name: conditional
examples.doc:
Conditional effect.
Wrap in If() to toggle reactively based on state.
examples.code:
dimmed := true
VBox(
	HBox(
		Text("● status").FG(Green),
		Text("  "),
		Text("████").FG(Cyan),
		Text("░░░░").FG(RGB(80, 80, 80)),
	),
	If(&dimmed).Then(ScreenEffect(SEDim())),
)

examples.name: multiple
examples.doc:
Stacked effects.
Effects apply in order, left to right — each sees the output of the previous.
examples.code:
VBox(
	HBox(
		Text("● red").FG(Red),
		Text("  "),
		Text("● green").FG(Green),
		Text("  "),
		Text("● blue").FG(Blue),
	),
	HBox(
		Text("████████").FG(RGB(255, 200, 50)),
		Text("████████").FG(RGB(50, 200, 255)),
	),
	ScreenEffect(
		SEDesaturate().Strength(0.5),
		SETint(Hex(0xFF6600)).Strength(0.1),
	),
)

constructors.doc:

	Textf("Name: ", Bold(&it.Name), " Status: ", &it.Status)  // ForEach compatible

	If(&mode).Eq("edit").Then(editor)       // show when equal
	If(&count).Ne(0).Then(badge).Else(Text("empty"))

If(&show).Then(Text("visible"))

types.name: DropShadowEffect
types.doc:
DropShadowEffect is a glow/drop-shadow — the inverse of vignette.
Where vignette darkens from the screen edges inward, this darkens outward
from a focus node's perimeter. At offset (0,0) it's a symmetric glow.
Any offset displaces the shadow source, giving a directional drop shadow.

constructors.name: SEDropShadow
constructors.doc:
SEDropShadow creates a radial glow/shadow emanating outward from a focus node.
Default: radius 8, strength 0.2, offset (-1,-1) for a subtle directional shadow.
Chain .Focus(&ref) to set the source node, .Offset(x,y) to adjust direction.

examples.doc: Directional drop shadow behind a panel.
examples.code:
var panel NodeRef
VBox(
	Text(""),
	HBox(
		Text("   "),
		VBox.Border(BorderRounded).NodeRef(&panel)(
			Text("shadowed panel").FG(Green),
			Text("████████").FG(Cyan),
		),
	),
	Text(""),
	Text(""),
	ScreenEffect(SEDropShadow().Focus(&panel)),
)

examples.name: glow
examples.doc: Symmetric glow — offset(0,0) centres the shadow source on the panel.
examples.code:
var panel NodeRef
VBox(
	Text(""),
	HBox(
		Text("   "),
		VBox.Border(BorderRounded).NodeRef(&panel)(
			Text("glowing panel").FG(RGB(255, 200, 50)),
			Text("████████").FG(RGB(255, 150, 50)),
		),
	),
	Text(""),
	Text(""),
	ScreenEffect(SEDropShadow().Focus(&panel).Offset(0, 0).Strength(0.4).Radius(12)),
)

methods.doc: Offset displaces the shadow source — turns the symmetric glow into a directional drop shadow.

T is comparable; ordered operators (Gt/Lt/Gte/Lte) constrain themselves

constructors.name: Match
constructors.doc:
Match builds a first-match-wins conditional block.
Each case is evaluated top-to-bottom; the first true case renders.
Chain .Default() to set a fallback when no case matches.

	Match(&cpu,
	    Gt(90.0, Text("CRITICAL").FG(Red)),
	    Gt(70.0, Text("WARNING").FG(Yellow)),
	    Where(func(v float64) bool { return v < 10 }, Text("COLD").FG(Blue)),
	).Default(Text("OK").FG(Green))

examples.doc:
First-match-wins conditional.
Evaluates cases top-to-bottom; the first true case renders.
examples.code:
status := "error"
Match(&status,
	Eq("ok", Text("all clear")),
	Eq("warn", Text("warning")),
	Eq("error", Text("failure")),
).Default(Text("unknown"))

examples.doc:
Ordered thresholds.
Order matters — the first matching case wins, so check the highest threshold first.
examples.code:
cpu := 85.0
Match(&cpu,
	Gt(90.0, Text("CRITICAL")),
	Gt(70.0, Text("WARNING")),
	Lte(70.0, Text("OK")),
)

	Where(func(q string) bool { return len(q) >= 3 }, Text("searching")),
)

types.name: Op

Op represents a single compiled template instruction.
The template compiler produces a flat array of these; Execute walks them to render.
types.decl:
type Op struct {
	Kind   OpKind
	Depth  int8  // tree depth (root children = 0)
	Parent int16 // parent op index, -1 for root children

	// Layout hints
	Width        int16   // explicit width
	Height       int16   // explicit height
	PercentWidth float32 // 0.0-1.0
	FlexGrow     float32 // share of remaining space
	Gap          int8    // gap between children
	ContentSized bool    // has fixed-width children (don't implicit flex)
	FitContent   bool    // size to content instead of filling available space

	// Container
	IsRow        bool        // true=HBox, false=VBox
	Border       BorderStyle // border style
	BorderFG     *Color      // border foreground color
	BorderBG     *Color      // border background color
	Title        string      // border title
	ChildStart   int16       // first child op index
	ChildEnd     int16       // last child op index (exclusive)
	CascadeStyle *Style      // style inherited by children (pointer for dynamic themes)
	LocalStyle   *Style      // style for this container only (not inherited)
	Fill         Color       // container fill color (fills entire area)
	Margin       [4]int16    // outer margin: top, right, bottom, left
	Padding      [4]int16    // inner padding: top, right, bottom, left
	NodeRef      *NodeRef    // if set, populated with rendered screen bounds each frame
	OpacityMode  OpacityMode // rune handoff strategy when OpDyn.Opacity is set

	// kind-specific data — type-assert based on Kind.
	// we use a Kind switch + type assertion instead of interface dispatch because
	// concrete method calls after assertion are inlinable. interface calls are not,
	// and cause parameters to escape to heap. verified via go build -gcflags='-m -m'.
	Ext any

	// dynamic layout property overrides — nil for static ops
	Dyn *OpDyn
}

types.name: SpinGlowEffect
types.doc:
SpinGlowEffect emanates a coloured halo around a focus node and rotates it.
N palette colours become N evenly-spaced stops around the ring, lerped between
neighbours. Angular intensity is also modulated so a bright arc traces the
perimeter — even a single-colour palette visibly spins.

constructors.name: SESpinGlow
constructors.doc:
SESpinGlow creates a rotating radial halo around a focus node. Pass zero
colours for the default palette, or one+ colours to define a conic gradient
of stops that rotates with time.

	SESpinGlow(&ref)                                 // default palette
	SESpinGlow(&ref, RGB(255, 80, 120))              // single-tint hotspot
	SESpinGlow(&ref, RGB(255,80,120), RGB(150,100,255)) // two-stop swirl

methods.name: Falloff
methods.doc:
Falloff shapes the halo's intensity curve between the rect and the radius.
0 = linear 1→0 (baseline). Higher values concentrate the drop-off closer
to the rect — intensity falls quickly just outside the rect, then trails
off more gently toward the radius. The curve is blended 50/50 with a
linear term so the halo stays visible all the way to the radius at every
Falloff value — Radius is declarative, it's always the visible disappearing
point regardless of the curve shape. fast-pathed for integer values 0..3.

methods.name: Opacity
methods.doc:
Opacity sets the compositor opacity for the whole spin glow effect. Unlike
Strength, this is intended for fades: it scales the halo and the foreground
rim without changing the fully-on rim solidity.

methods.name: OpacityMode
methods.doc:
OpacityMode sets how rim cells hand back to backing runes as effect opacity
fades. The default is OpacityPaint so a mostly-opaque rim remains solid.

methods.name: PaletteRef
methods.doc:
PaletteRef wires a per-frame palette source. The pointer is dereferenced
each Apply, so callers can swap the palette live just by reassigning the
slice variable the pointer addresses — no effect rebuild required.
When set, supersedes the palette passed at construction.

methods.name: Radius
methods.doc: Radius sets how far the glow spreads in cells.

methods.name: Rim
methods.doc:
Rim enables painting the focus node's border perimeter with the rotating
conic palette — analogous to a CSS conic-gradient stroke on a border.
Overrides existing border FG. Use on containers with a visible border for
a rotating-rim look; pair with a small Radius for "rim with a soft outer
halo" that mirrors the glyph-website install pill.

methods.name: Speed
methods.doc: Speed sets rotation speed in radians per second. Zero freezes the glow.

methods.name: Strength
methods.doc: Strength sets how strongly the glow blends into surrounding cells (0..1).

Custom layout.
Arrange lets you define a fully custom layout function. It receives child sizes and available space, returns rects.

funcs.name: In
funcs.doc:
In marks the active value used while a conditional branch is present.
Pass a tween to animate in, or a plain value to snap in and only animate out.

examples.doc:
Enter and exit transitions.
Wrap any property value with In for the entry and Out for the exit. Pass a
tween to either side to animate it; pass a plain value to snap. Both sides
are tied to the surrounding conditional, and Glyph keeps the outgoing branch
on screen until its Out tween completes.

NodeOpacity returns a node ref's effective rendered opacity. Refs without an
opacity-producing ancestor are treated as fully opaque.

funcs.name: RuneCount
funcs.doc:
RuneCount returns the number of runes in s. Use this when you need a
character count (e.g. indexing into a rune slice), not a display width.

funcs.name: RuneWidth
funcs.doc:
RuneWidth returns the display-cell width of a rune. ASCII is width 1 on the
fast path; anything above U+1100 defers to the runewidth table. Zero-width
runes (combining marks) are reported as 1 because terminals treat them as
advancing the cursor by 1 in most cases.

funcs.name: StringWidth
funcs.doc: StringWidth returns the total display-cell width of s.
